utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: A very good morning to everybody. Behind the scenes, in particular when it's that early, but we read that we must have another Status Conference before Easter. May I ask you, Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-00-39-A, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And may I ask the appearances, please for the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: May it please the Court I am Christine Dahl and with me today is Shelagh McCall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I am Colin Nicholls for Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, and as usual we have as interpreter ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Karganovic, Stefan Karganovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, Stefan Karganovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I turn immediately to you, Mr. Krajisnik, with two questions first. Can you follow the proceedings in a language you understand and at the same time do you have any complaints as regards your health situation or the situation in the Detention Unit? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can follow the proceedings in my own language, and I don't have any complaints about my health situation or the situation in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The number of motions and documents before the Appeals Chamber is increasing, so let's try not to forget anything and to have some order. First of all, let me say that I'm extremely grateful for both parties having brought submissions, Prosecution in relation to the question of self-representation on appeal. Prosecution requested that the Appeals Chamber substitute the attached brief in full. That was the brief of the 3rd of April, 2007. This is so granted. Then we also got the submissions by Mr. Nicholls on the question of amici curiae or amicus curiae in the concrete case on the higher level. I'm also grateful for this. And then finally, admittedly a little bit out of surprise, yesterday late in the evening I received a letter dated Monday, 2 April 2007, from Mr. Krajisnik himself where it reads in the subject, "Complaint concerning self-representation." Mr. Krajisnik, may I ask you, when did you send this letter to the Registry? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] On Monday I wrote the letter, and I intended to give it to Mr. Karganovic to translate it, for you to receive it translated. In the Detention Unit they would not allow me to do that, and they told me that I could send the letter directly to you. The day before yesterday, i.e., on Tuesday, I gave the letter to somebody to send it to you, and I fully expected that you would receive the letter on the same day, on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I did not and I'm not quite sure whether the parties did. We tried to do it by e-mail yesterday. The one sent to Mr. Nicholls came back. May I ask the registrar, please, to distribute copies of this letter dated Monday, the 2nd of April, 2007, in its English version to all participants.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I provided Mr. Nicholls a copy of this morning given that he's here from out of town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can see the party-driven system has also some advantages, and thank you very much for this. But to go into the details. The question before us today and the same question was before us already during the last Status Conference that we know unambiguously what is your desire, to represent yourself, or to be represented by your Defence team in an open way, or whether you would opt for Mr. Nicholls as continued assigned counsel. The last time I recall, you said that you would contact Mr. -- Professor Stojanovic from Belgrade to take over the appeals proceedings. May I ask, in which way did you contact Professor Stojanovic? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Immediately after the end of the Status Conference, on several occasions I tried and finally managed to get hold of Professor Stojanovic over the phone. To my deep regret, he was not able to come to The Hague, and he was not able to accept the role of the lead counsel in this case. In my letter, I have quoted his reasons for which he has decided not to be the lead counsel and while he accepted to be a member of my team should I decide to represent myself, I can give you those reasons briefly. The first reason is that after our last conversation which took place in March when he was willing to come and discuss the terms of him taking over the case, I had to call him after that and tell him that he couldn't come because this was not in compliance with the provisions laid out by the Registry. In the meantime, he has taken over some other obligations because he's an a full-time professor. The second reason why he couldn't be here even for one day is twofold. The first one is the fact that a his visa has expired, and the second reason is that immediately prior to our conversation his mother had a brain stroke and he has to look after her. So, Your Honour, this would be my answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let me ask you, did you request for a supervised telephone call or was it an open phone call, an uncontrolled phone call? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] The telephone conversation was an uncontrolled phone call. I didn't use the privileges of a supervised call. Truth be told, I -- it never even occurred to me to ask for a privileged line with Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As we discuss the last time, you got the specific allowance of to have a discussion unsupervised for about 15 minutes in the Detention Unit itself, but apparently you were allowed to have an uncontrolled telephone call with a member, as you call it yourself in the letter, a member of your Defence team. So -- but in conclusion as regards Professor Stojanovic, he's unable to appear as your Defence right now; correct? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] This is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it furthermore correct that then later on you tried to engage the services of Mr. Dejan Brasic also over the phone? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] A minor correction if I may, please. When I arrived -- may I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] When I arrived in the Detention Unit, I received a decision by the Registry in English that the Prosecution announced preventing Mr. Brasic from being engaged as my Defence counsel. I called him also in an uncontrolled manner, on an uncontrolled line, and since I knew that he could not be engaged, I expressed my regret for possibly having contributed to his fine by asking for him to be my Defence counsel. We finished this conversation with an understanding that he could not act as my Defence counsel because of the obstacles posed by the Registry. And I repeat again, this conversation was also an uncontrolled one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. But was it already clarified during the last Status Conference that Mr. Brasic is not able for the reasons we all know to be -- to appear before this Tribunal any longer? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. The Prosecution stated that, and the decision on the -- serve to confirm that this was not possible. I understood it last time that a decision had been reached, but I did not receive it myself until a few days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't want to go into details of the background, why Mr. Brasic can't appear any longer. It's a decision taken by the Registry and by a Trial Chamber as regards the fine. In conclusion, I have to ask you, Mr. Krajisnik, whenever you want to address the Chamber, please don't do it personally in addressing a letter to me myself but to the entire Chamber. As it is custom in our Tribunal, let it be filed. And you have also an assigned -- properly assigned counsel, Mr. Nicholls, and Mr. Nicholls would take care of this in order to avoid any delay. However, having heard your submissions, I expect a report from the Registrar no later than 12th of April on two issues. First, how is it possible that Mr. Krajisnik had contact with two members of his so-called Defence team from the United Nations Detention Unit without any control, without any monitoring. And second, why is it that the letter arrived only by the end of office hours yesterday, because having had the letter beforehand, I could have taken the appropriate steps and prepared this Status Conference in a totally different way. This letter is extremely short, and I think within 10 or 15 minutes with the assistance of a translator I could at least have got a gist of that, of what is included. So I'm -- was only able to respond or to think about the content of this letter late yesterday evening. So now we have the situation Mr. Dershowitz is not available. Mr. Brasic can't defend you. Professor Stojanovic, for at least the time being, is not - in part able, in part willing - to take over your defence. May I therefore ask you, and I think if I'm wrong please correct me, you know the conditions of self-representation as highlighted in all detail in the last Status Conference by Mr. Petrov to you. Is it correct that you know all the conditions, or shall I repeat them? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I would be grateful to you if you could go over these conditions again. One thing still remains unclear to me, and this thing has to do with the remuneration of the Defence team. I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it was made abundantly clear that in this case, as things stand now, you have an assigned counsel and this counsel is paid by the international taxpayer, if you would decide to defend yourself, then it would really mean that you have to defend yourself. There would be no financial support from the side of the Tribunal. In particular, costs for legal advisors, investigators, and so on will not be covered. As regards the question of privileged access to confidential information and to enjoy unsupervised visits, in particular -- and all the other means emanating from the right to have uncontrolled visits by counsel, the so-called counsel/client privilege, this has to be decided on a case-by-case basis, and primarily this person would have to fulfil certain criteria listed in the code of conduct for Defence counsel. But as I said in the beginning, the Tribunal will not tolerate so-called undercover defence. We fight or searching -- we are searching for the truth and searching for justice by open means, with open weapons, and not in a disguised way. I think it's clear enough. Defending yourself means at the same time if you would want to invoke this right and the -- of course the Appeals Chamber would have to decide on this, all the costs have to be borne by you yourself. And to be abundantly clear, today is the last opportunity after, I think, more than six months that you finally decide whether you request to represent yourself during appeal or not. I'm not prepared to continue with the same game we had with Mr. Alan Dershowitz and now with, unfortunately, Professor Stojanovic, but we need an immediate and final and, first of all, unequivocal decision on your part. May I ask, do you have any further questions before you give a clear answer to this clear question? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in my letter I have also concluded a request which I may explain with regard to Mr. Dershowitz, and I'm going to give you a clear answer as regards my self-representation. At this moment, I wish to represent myself, and I cannot accept Mr. Nicholls as representing me in this appeals case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, may I come back to the last Status Conference of Monday, 26 March 2007. In the English version of the not official, not corrected transcript it reads at page 32, Mr. Krajisnik, you said, I quote as from line 8: "At the moment there are investigators who were members of the first team, and there are certain items for which we would have to engage two Defence lawyers who would analyse in professional terms the appeal. I cannot do this myself, and it would be necessary for me to have the possibility of receiving e-mail for both the Defence lawyers and for the investigators." Then you continue -- end of this quote. You continue on line 16: "I'm convinced that I can defend myself in more professional way than the team that I currently have could do, but I believe that the appeal procedure is specific, and I would need counsel's assistance to deal with this appeals procedure. So when I'm defending myself, I would like to have a very experienced lawyer as a member of the Defence team." We are still in a situation -- end of quote. We are still in the situation that you, on the one hand, cite, claim, that you want to defend yourself, but on the other hand, you claim that you need a Defence team for these purposes, in particular, a very experienced lawyer as a member of the Defence team, in particular with a view to the difficulties of the appeals proceedings. And you continue on page 33 of the same transcript, lines 2 to 4 -- or 1 to 4: "There are three individuals, and in addition there would be the investigators who have been working on the case so far. That would be my Defence team, the team that would assist me and with which I would prepare for the appellate proceedings." So do you believe that you are able to defend yourself, as you stated in your letter, or do you believe that you have to rely on a Defence team as you said, in particular, a "very experienced lawyer" for your assistance? What is correct? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this Tribunal and with the Judges and the lawyers, the problem is always the same. The problem is that the freedom of expression -- one's freedom of expression is restricted. My freedom of expression is restricted. I'll be very clear now. I'm now stating that I want to represent myself. I want to defend myself because I believe this is the best and most efficient way me to establish what the truth is. I have already said that I cannot accept Mr. Nicholls as counsel. I can provide you with an explanation but I would rather not do so. As far as my statement is concerned, the statement I made last time we had a Status Conference. This case represents an enormous workload and one person alone cannot deal with this workload. Even if other lawyers were involved this couldn't be done. I believe that I need a number of individuals to help me in these appellate proceedings, and if I am to engage someone, in that case I would like to engage someone who is professional, someone who can deal with the procedural matters here and can help in drafting and submitting an appeal. I don't want to involve Mr. Dershowitz in this now, but I can explain to you what I had in mind last time. I can explain how my initial position has evolved a bit. I'm repeating that I believe that it would be far more efficient for me to defend myself. I can file an appeal. I can become involved in the appellate proceedings. I just need the right conditions. But without such conditions I think it will be very difficult for me to work on my appeal since there are so many factors of a restrictive nature. That's all I have to say for the moment, Mr. -- Your Honour. If you have any questions, I can answer them, but I think that I'm in a position to represent myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And before -- Sorry, before I give the floor to the Prosecution, I saw all the time you were about to be on your foot, I want to clarify that we can get rid of this letter of 2nd April. Your last question clearly falls in the jurisdiction of the Registry, but I can already now tell you based on the experience of the past that the Registry would never assign Mr. Dershowitz and grant him in addition -- that you "grant him in addition to the funds provided by the Registrar which are designated for covering attorney expenses and shall only be used for that purposes to allow you to participate in the financing in -- of my defence with my own funds. These funds would be provided by loans, and donations would cover additional activities which were not carried out during the presentation of evidence ..." You will get the final answer on this last part of your answer by the Registry in due time. But to make one thing abundantly clear, it is not possible to claim that you want to defend yourself and, on the other hand, that you want to have a Defence team somewhere behind the scenes. But let me give me now the floor to the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution's interest is in ensuring that the fairness of the proceedings is not impaired. I wanted to interject that before Mr. Krajisnik was asked whether his request to represent himself was unequivocal, and it seems to -- continues to be the opposite, that is equivocal or conditional, that it would be essential to that exercise of the right, if he has such, to make sure that he is fully informed of the dangers of self-representation. Many commentators have observed that self-representation is at tension with the fairness of the appellate proceedings and that it is in effect a waiver of the fairness of the proceedings for the convicted person to exercise his self-representation rights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I can only -- speaking for the time being for myself as a Judge of the Bench, I can only repeat what I said the last time, that when you compare the situation in different countries all over the world and before international tribunals, because of the difficulties in principle and in particular in some countries on appeal, there is no such right of self-representation, and I quoted already from the Farhad decision of the United States Supreme Court, Judge Reinhardt saying in stating in a concurring opinion that, "allowing on appeal an appellant to represent himself would amount to a waiver of a fair trial." You should also bear this, please, in mind before deciding. But one point concerned me in your last submission earlier this morning when you said that you are deprived of your freedom of expression. Could you please elaborate a little bit on this? And what has this to do with yourself representation or being presented by Defence counsel? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Well, in fact I want to actively participate in my defence, even if I was represented by counsel, but at this point in time, now that I'm defending myself, it's important for me to have contact with individuals who will obtain certain documents for me. I'm deeply surprised now, since I wouldn't have the right to assistant of any kind from my investigators or from anyone else. I'd have to defend myself by drafting my appeals brief in the Detention Unit. If that's a fair trial -- well, I don't think it is. I believed I needed a team who could assist me. And to go back to your question, Your Honour, I cannot now send a fax, for example, to have Mr. Karganovic translate something for me. I have to go through a lawyer whom I don't recognise as my lawyer. Secondly, I have to receive CDs of documents that relate to sessions of an Assembly to see whether what was said was actually said, to see whether the transcript was correct. I can't obtain this material. I have to send something by mail, for example. I have to receive a 7 or 800-page document, and this is not possible. So none of these conditions currently exist. I don't have the conditions that would enable me to communicate with individuals to communicate with them and to gather evidence in order to draft my appeals brief. Until this issue of self-defence is solved, I'm told I can't do anything. I have to communicate with Mr. Nicholls. I have to be quite frank. On three occasions to date I saw Mr. Nicholls very briefly. I haven't seen, though, what submissions he has made. Being a polite person, I communicated with him to a certain extent, but at this point in time there's nothing I can do. I don't have a judgement in the Serbian language, so I more or less have to try and translate the judgement by frequently consulting a dictionary in order to work on -- on the appeal. But such are the Rules, and the Rules are imposing restrictions on me. It's not the individuals who are involved in all this who are to blame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, you didn't answer my question in how far you feel deprived of your right to self-expression. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I cannot prepare my defence in good conditions. That's what I want to say. I didn't want to say that anyone was obstructing me or I wasn't trying to say that my rights had been violated. That's the only thing. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Isn't it correct that in your home country it is mandatory to have Defence counsel in a case like the one before us? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I am not familiar with those details, but there is something that I do know, Your Honour. In my home country, the accused and counsel sit together, and they put questions together, and they conduct the proceedings together. I know about that. And if this was the case here, things would be much better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And in addition, am I correct in believing that as in your country as in many other continental European countries you have the right at the same time to have counsel and to put questions to witnesses and to make statements other than those foreseen in our Rules and procedure -- of Procedure and Evidence? Is that correct? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] There is certainly that possibility but, Your Honour, there's one important factor in my homeland, and a minute ago you said this wasn't possible here. If I could engage Mr. Dershowitz, if the Registry engaged him, all problems would be solved, but it's obvious that Mr. Dershowitz is requesting certain conditions that can't be met or that won't be met, and I would have to find additional funds. In my home country I could solve this, but I can't solve this problem here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. I think we have discussed now everything, but I have not yet given the floor to Mr. Nicholls, and he should also have the right as an assigned counsel to make submissions. I think based on your additional submission in writing on amicus curiae, we need not discuss this any further because I think the question of amicus curiae is finally litigated and this question is right for a decision, but I see the Prosecution again was faster than the Defence. Please, the floor is yours.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I wish to make three points and one housekeeping matter. In listening to Mr. Krajisnik's elocution, it appears to me that he has already described himself as self-represented. It would appear that that is premature and that perhaps it would be appropriate to remind him that he is represented in this matter as it stands. Second, there appears to be a misunderstanding. If he were able to retain his own lawyer and fund his own Defence team, he would have the ability to manage their work himself subject to the detention centre rules and the qualifications necessary for people to appear as retained counsel in this Tribunal. Finally, the statements May Mr. Krajisnik has made concerning the nature of his relationship with Mr. Nicholls cause concern. Those may be appropriate subjects of investigation ex parte to the Prosecution if Mr. Nicholls continues to represent Mr. Krajisnik. As to the housekeeping matter, I wish to note a correction to the transcript at page 8, line 37 [sic] where I indicated that the Prosecution's interest is in ensuring that the fairness of the proceedings is not impaired. Presently the transcript does not include the negative word "not."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification, and may I ask those being responsible for the transcript to correct the transcript to this end. As regards to your first point that will be the final point to be addressed after having heard Mr. Nicholls, but you're absolutely right. Apart from those scenarios I highlighted, which are possible, which are no-go's, there is the possibility to have Defence counsel based on own funds or donations or own money if Mr. Krajisnik should be in possession of the necessary financial means. But I think it goes without saying that Mr. Krajisnik is intelligent enough to know this. But may I hear finally Mr. Nicholls, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour has before you Mr. Krajisnik's application to represent himself, and at the same time his application that he should have legal assistance, and he has indicated, apart from the fact that he does not wish that assistance to be from me, he has indicated that the assistance he wants is assistance on procedure and assisting -- assistance on the drafting of documents as a member of his team, as has been described an undercover team. That assistance Mr. Krajisnik is seeking is not assistance which is within the remit of an assigned Defence counsel or within the remit of a lead counsel. Counsel has specific responsibilities. He has responsibilities as to what he himself does, and he has responsibility for his team. He must also, in accordance with Article 10 of the code, he must ensure that he has an independence. He forms the team. It is his team which he controls for the benefit of Mr. Krajisnik. What Mr. Krajisnik is seeking is that I should be, I and those assisting me, which he wishes to approve, should be part of his team and inevitably not really subject to his instructions but subject to his control. I have to say, and I have to make it clear for the benefit of the Chamber and for the benefit of Mr. Krajisnik that that is not a role which I envisage as one which I, as his Defence counsel, can fulfil. Your Honour asked me on the last occasion, was I willing to work with his team as he described it, and I indicated very clearly no, that I could not do so for the very reasons which I have indicated to Your Honour. Your Honour has already indicated that matter of [indiscernible] has been fully litigated in previous decisions of the Chambers and also, of course, fully argued on the last occasion. I cannot think that I can add anything to that. Your Honour asked me a question, was amicus not a friend of the Court, effectively independent of the defendant, and I feel bound to admit that in truth in reality that is the position. There are, of course, in the United States or in the United Kingdom there are amicus briefs which are submitted. They are amicus briefs which are presented by persons other than the parties, although they may in fact be in support of the parties. And I think unless Your Honour asks me to address any other issue, I can't really add anything at this moment. But I have to be really very clear about it, that if I am counsel I take the responsibility, and I have the control. I cannot be subject to the control of the person I represent in the way in which is envisaged. I cannot draft documents, that is, put into some formal shape documents which the client has drafted and which he wants to have presented in a suitable form to the Tribunal. That, as I see it, is not the function of counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for these clear words, Mr. Nicholls, and I can only repeat that Defence means not only to have rights but also obligations and, in your words, a responsibility both for the proper defence but also in order to protect victims, witnesses, and other protective measures ordered, say, under Rule 70 by this Tribunal. So therefore, I first want to give you, Mr. Krajisnik, a last chance. You heard from the submissions of the Prosecution that the Prosecution still believes that your submission is not unequivocal. This would be a prerequisite for a clear request for self-representation. You heard the words of Mr. Nicholls, the counsel assigned to you, and I have to emphasise as the President said, properly assigned Defence counsel. Do you seek still a decision of the Appeals Chamber could -- on the first question whether your request is unequivocal, and second, whether you are entitled to represent yourself on appeal or it is for the entire Appeal Chamber, of course, to decide this, whether the -- you can't waive your right to have a fair trial. What is your final request, please? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] My position is absolutely clear. I want to represent myself, and I believe that this would be far better. The trial would be a lot fairer than if I decided to select someone to represent me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krajisnik. You may be seated. Then it remains with the status quo we have at present that properly assigned counsel to Mr. Krajisnik is and will be Mr. Nicholls until Appeals Chamber has decided on Mr. Krajisnik's request to represent himself and/or whether this request was unequivocal or not. This also means that you, and I have to emphasise and I have to kindly ask you to regard your position not as an amicus curiae but as a properly assigned Defence counsel. Having been compelled myself by my own bar several times to defend a client against his wish, and this happens relatively often, I know how difficult this is, but in the interest of justice this sometimes is inevitable. And it is really for you, Mr. Krajisnik, to make the best of it, and I can only recommend to try to get a better contact to Mr. Nicholls, because in the near future nothing will change -- will be changed until the Appeals Chamber has spoken. Let us now move to the pending motions. Let's go, please, briefly in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. For reason that easy to understand, we are confronted with a Defence motion for extension of time for filing appellate brief pending translation of the judgement into the language of the convicted person. If I'm right, please correct me if it's not the case. You ask for 90 additional days?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, it was, I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I hear the Prosecution on this?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the motion requested 75 days. Our submission was that it is in the interests of justice to grant that; however, we would request that it's limited to 30 days after receipt of the judgement in Mr. Krajisnik's native language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. This is not an oriental bazaar, and we should stay in line of previous decisions, and I looked up previous decisions and indeed there were either 30 or 25 days granted. The last time in another case I granted 25 days after filing of the B/C/S translation, bearing in the mind -- bearing in mind that the -- that Mr. Nicholls can work in the meantime on the main body of the appeal brief, and it is only to add something based on that what he hopefully gets as information. I emphasise information, not instruction, from Mr. Krajisnik. So therefore it is hereby granted that the time for filing the appellate brief is extended 25 days after filing of the B/C/S translation of the judgement to Mr. Krajisnik. It is therefore up to you, Mr. Nicholls, to continue with this. The only point that strikes me is the pending motion to strike Mr. Krajisnik's notice of appeal. I think it would be a matter of fairness, but of course I have to hear first the parties on this, whether it wouldn't be wise if Mr. Nicholls would look into Mr. Krajisnik's own notice of appeal and maybe file a consolidated version of his own notice of appeal and Mr. Krajisnik's notice of appeal so that Mr. Krajisnik's requests are also included in as far your -- your tactics and your ethical obligations so allow. It would have to be decided until when such a consolidated version would be to be filed. May I hear the Prosecution first on whether at all they would accept this and, second, whether a time for such a consolidated version of, say, of -- bearing in mind that we have Easter right now, to grant a time a fortnight running from next Monday for such a consolidated version? What is your opinion on this?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wish to clarify that our motion directed at Mr. Krajisnik's notice of appeal was not a request to strike it so much as a request that the registrar not accept a filing from an individual while he is represented by counsel. That position information the answer to your question, which is that we don't oppose an amended notice of appeal by counsel, but we remain firm in the position that one party, one document, and that we should not have a two-track appeal where the convicted person is taking his own matters himself while represented by competent counsel as Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it goes without saying into we have only two parties in this system, but nevertheless we are confronted with the difficulty situation that the Appeals Chamber has not yet decided on -- finally on the question of self-representation or not and is, therefore, in order not to waste time, Mr. Krajisnik himself and Mr. Nicholls was allowed to file two separate notices of appeal, but as I take it now from your submission, you don't see any obstacle that a consolidated version will be filed. Mr. Nicholls, would you be ready to do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've always contemplated a consolidated notice of appeal. The only request that I would make is that Your Honour should grant more time, rather, three weeks instead of two weeks having regard to the difficulties of communication aunts fact that the teams are in fact in different places. When I say the teams are in different places, the team is in London, Mr. Krajisnik is here, and there are always the problems of communication which Your Honour is aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And I take it that you will take the advantage of the interpretation services as you highlighted correctly during the last Status Conference of your colleague sitting behind you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe. I say no more at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. But you will find ways and means to --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: There will be -- there will be interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Let me think loudly. Today we have 5 April, and you are requesting three weeks. That would bring us to 26, 27 of April. In case that this does not cause any further delay, I think it could be granted but let me hear -- first hear the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: We agree with the motion that there should be no further extensions if this is granted to Mr. Nicholls, this further week. The purpose of the notice of appeal of course is to allow the Prosecution to begin to prepare its response, and we have been diligently doing that in reliance on the extant notice of appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. I think this work was not in vain because this will still form part of the notice of appeal. It will be only amended by adding maybe the one or other ground of appeal raised by Mr. Krajisnik himself. So, Mr. Nicholls, would it be convenient for you to accept on the one hand that the appeals brief as such is due 25 days after filing of the B/C/S translation of the judgement, and at the same time that a consolidated version of both notices of appeal will be filed no later than 26 April 2007?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you so much. May I ask what about other pending motions? Maybe you know that I don't like unnecessary filings, so that we can dispose of any pending motions right now. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you please be seated. You are represented properly by Defence counsel. I'll give you the floor in the minute, even though this is not foreseen in -- in the Rules. I was asking you about other pending motions. I think the motion to strike will become moot as soon we have a consolidated version of -- from Mr. Nicholls; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it -- please, and this is for both parties, correct me if I'm wrong, we have before us the motion on self-representation, and may I ask based on the current new situation do you uphold your motion for becoming a permanent institution as amicus curiae, Mr. Nicholls? Because this was a motion filed by you in your own capacity.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, when I was faced with the situation that Mr. Krajisnik did not accept me as his assigned counsel, I formed a team and I filed a number of motions in order to protect his situation. One was that I should no longer be assigned; two, that he should be allowed to self-represent; and thirdly, that the Court -- the Chamber should consider whether I and my team, as I described it, should be made amicus. I think during the last Status Conference it was clear effectively that the position of amicus was so very different from the position of a Defence counsel and that the position of amicus did not include what Mr. Krajisnik was requesting. I have filed that motion that I and my team -- or that the Chamber should consider whether I and my team should be appointed amicus. I -- I leave it -- in some ways I would like time to answer the question, because I want to preserve Mr. Krajisnik's position. But at the same time, and may I just say frankly that I have an inclination not to pursue the motion for this reason, that I would not wish that I should be placed in a position whereas an amicus, as not an amicus in the ordinary sense of the term, I was required to give Mr. Krajisnik the assistance which he has been requesting, that is in the drafting of documents and the like, which I do not -- or submit is not the normal or proper function of an amicus. So Your Honour asked me a direct question. I've answered in a rather roundabout way, but would Your Honour give me time to consider the answer to the question whether the motion is pursued or not? I can give -- I can give an answer by the end of the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I -- as Easter is upcoming, I would say if you do be kind enough to file your motion whether or not you want to withdraw your motion to be assigned as amicus curiae no later than Friday next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I can looking forward to this. And I can only repeat that you are the assigned counsel. You have to work with your team, and everything falls in your own responsibility. And furthermore, I have to ask the Registry to take the necessary steps that there are no contacts not foreseen in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence between Mr. Krajisnik and any counsel at all. Of course it may be that there is a supervised visit by and friend, a member of the family, but this has nothing to do with defence or, as Mr. Krajisnik tends to call it, Defence team, because there is as things stand now no such Defence team of Mr. Krajisnik. Mr. Krajisnik, in all fairness, you wanted to say something. Please, you're allowed to do so right now. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] If I may, I would like to provide an explanation about your last order. Last time you granted me the right to replace my Defence counsel if I was of the opinion that the current Defence counsel is not suitable. How can I get in touch with any prospective Defence counsel if I'm not allowed to make telephone calls? That's my first question. And the second thing I wish to say is this: In order to avoid any misunderstandings, I certainly wish to self-represent. I'm saying this because it arised from you -- it arose from your conclusion that there's a doubt whether I really want to self-represent or not. Second of all, just for the record, I am against and joint notice of appeal or a consolidated notice of appeal, because I did not participated in the notice of appeal prepared by Mr. Nicholls. I received it very late, and I have a lot of objections to it. Again, to avoid any misunderstandings, if Mr. Nicholls is appointed as amicus curiae, I don't expect any favours of him. When I asked him about his role, I just wanted to see what this implied, and I was in favour of him in role as an amicus curiae if this is of some use for the Trial Chamber. I don't want him to be a member of my team at the same time as an amicus curiae. I have to work on my appeal, and I have to get in touch with my Defence team. Just for the record, Mr. Nicholls has not showed -- shown any willingness to contact me in this regard. I have not had any contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, if -- if I may interject. The Prosecution does not wish to be privy to matters of privilege between Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Nicholls that concern the nature of the representation or Mr. Nicholls's or Mr. Krajisnik's objections thereto.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we had -- have litigated this matter in a really exhaustive and extraordinary way. You had already the privilege for more than six months to request a counsel of your own choosing from the lists of the Registrar, and unfortunately you did not decide until today. So therefore, I take it that it is a matter -- mission impossible for you to find the appropriate counsel. It is, therefore, that counsel was assigned to you. You will get hopefully in due time the decision of the Appeals Chamber on your request of -- to represent yourself, but as things stay now, I on a very personal note have to add I don't believe that this Appeals Chamber will be in your hands, that you can control the course of action of this appeal. We have to grant you a fair trial, meaning also an expeditious trial. You are not the only one waiting for a final decision, and therefore time has come to conclude this debate, and if there is no other decision in the future, Mr. Nicholls will stay your assigned counsel, and it's in your own interests to find a way of trust to Mr. Nicholls. Otherwise, it will be detriment to your own interests. This concludes -- as I can see no other issues to be raised from any the parties, this concludes today's Status Conference. You will get the necessary decisions, and I'm expecting a consolidated version of the notice of appeal and then later on the appeal on brief. It remains for me to wish you all some days of relief and a happy Easter to all of you in this courtroom and those assisting us behind the scenes. Thank you very much. The Status Conference stands adjourned.
